question.title: Camera-body mechanics.
question.question: Reference-only question for the Leica M10 film study: which two visible cues distinguish camera-body mechanical assembly? Give a short answer from the guide.
question.answer: The cues to distinguish camera-body mechanical assembly are the visibility of an open camera body or a mechanical subassembly and observation of hands or a tool acting on that assembly. Since no visual observation is available, confirmation of these cues is not possible.
question.spoken_text: The cues to distinguish camera-body mechanical assembly are the visibility of an open camera body or a mechanical subassembly and observation of hands or a tool acting on that assembly.

question.title: Sensor-surface handling.
question.question: Reference-only question for the Leica M10 film study: what does the sensor-handling stage ask me to observe, and what remains unverified? Give a short answer from the guide.
question.answer: The sensor-handling stage asks you to observe the close handling or examination of an exposed sensor-like rectangular optical surface. Currently, it remains unverified whether the surface, hands, or implements are visibly present during the action.
question.spoken_text: The sensor-handling stage asks you to observe the close handling or examination of an exposed sensor-like rectangular optical surface.

question.title: Enclosure closure.
question.reference_topic: Alignment and fitting of the outer cover
question.question: Reference-only question for the Leica M10 film study: what enclosure-closure evidence should I look for, and does fitting the cover prove the camera works? Give a short answer from the guide.
question.answer: For the enclosure closure, look for the visible alignment and fitting of a shell or plate onto the partly assembled camera body, and ensure it covers previously exposed internals. Fitting the cover alone does not prove the camera functions correctly.
